subheadline: The 22-year-old slugger won the NL award after a 32-homer season that put him next to some of the biggest names in Cincinnati history.

body: Sal Stewart is the best rookie in the National League. The Cincinnati Reds first baseman won the 2026 NL Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year award on Nov. 9, collecting 20 of 30 first-place votes and 170 points. He was the only player named on every ballot.
Mets outfielder Carson Benge finished second with 107 points, and Cardinals infielder JJ Wetherholt was third.
## Why fans are buying in

Stewart's numbers would stand out in any season. He hit 32 home runs, drove in more than 110 runs and played all 162 games at age 22. He led NL rookies in homers, RBIs, extra-base hits and total bases, and he made the All-Star team.

His season also landed him in the Reds' record book. MLB.com notes he is the only Cincinnati rookie to reach 30 homers and 100 RBIs, he set the club's rookie RBI record, and his 164 hits were the most by a Reds rookie since Pete Rose in 1963.
The company he joins is a big part of the appeal. Stewart is the ninth Reds player to win the award, a list that includes Frank Robinson, Pete Rose, Johnny Bench and Jonathan India.

Cincinnati won 75 games and finished last in the NL Central, so fans are looking for a reason to be excited about what comes next. In our analysis, a young slugger who just won a national award is exactly the kind of player fans rally around and want to wear. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
Stewart wears No. 27. The banner above shows the classic white Reds home jersey with the red wordmark, the look most Cincinnati fans picture first.
## Why this jersey will last

Stewart has years of team control ahead, and he can play first, second and third base, which keeps him in the lineup every day. body: Kevin McGonigle ran away with it. The Detroit Tigers infielder won the 2026 AL Jackie Robinson Rookie of the Year award on Nov. 9, taking 28 of 30 first-place votes and 204 of a possible 210 points.
Cleveland pitcher Parker Messick was a distant second with 122 points, and Boston's Payton Tolle finished third.
## Why fans are buying in
McGonigle did a little of everything. He hit .278 with 18 homers, 72 RBIs, 97 runs, 28 doubles and 12 steals, and he drew 95 walks against 100 strikeouts. He played most of the season at 21.

The advanced numbers back it up. His 7.1 WAR by Baseball Reference's measure was the best among AL position players, per MLB.com. He is also the first rookie since Ted Williams in 1939 to reach at least 97 runs, 28 doubles, 18 homers, 72 RBIs and 95 walks.
He did it while splitting time almost evenly between shortstop and third base. The BBWAA notes only one earlier winner, Tony Kubek in 1957, did the same.

McGonigle is the sixth Tigers Rookie of the Year, joining Harvey Kuenn, Mark Fidrych, Lou Whitaker, Justin Verlander and Michael Fulmer. Verlander made his final start in September, and Detroit fans now have a new young face to follow. In our analysis, that handoff is the kind of moment that turns a promising rookie into the jersey a fan base picks up. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look
McGonigle wears No. 7. The banner above shows the white Tigers home jersey with the Old English D, one of the most recognizable looks in baseball.
## Why this jersey will last

Detroit went 76-86 and missed the playoffs, so the team is building around young players, and McGonigle is now the center of that plan. subheadline: The reigning Rookie of the Year scored 30 of his season-high 43 after halftime as Dallas came back to beat Indiana for a third straight win.

body: Cooper Flagg carried the Dallas Mavericks back from 10 down at halftime. He scored a season-high 43 points, 30 of them after the break, as Dallas beat the Indiana Pacers 125-122 at American Airlines Center on Nov. 9.
He made 16 of 25 shots and all eight of his free throws, and he added 10 rebounds, six assists and three steals.
## Why fans are buying in
The win was Dallas's third in a row and completed a 3-0 homestand. At 7-4, the Mavericks are three games over .500 for the first time since March 2025, per CBS Texas.

Flagg is also playing with a star beside him. Kyrie Irving, back this season after 19 months out with a torn ACL, scored 35 and hit seven 3-pointers. The two combined for 26 fourth-quarter points, including the team's first 13 of the period.

This is what Dallas hoped for when it drafted Flagg first overall in 2025. He won Rookie of the Year last season with 56 first-place votes after averaging 21.0 points, and the 43 points were his fourth straight double-double. He is still only 19.
## The look

Flagg wears No. 32. The banner above shows his blue Icon Edition, the white Association Edition and the navy Statement Edition, so fans can choose between the classic home look and the darker alternate.
## Why this jersey will last

Fans already bought in during his rookie year. Flagg ranked ninth on the NBA's top-selling jersey list for the 2025-26 regular season, based on NBAStore.com and Fanatics sales, and was the only rookie on it. In our analysis, a second-year star leading a team that is winning again should keep that support growing. That last part is our view, not a sales figure.
